physiology:
The traditions seat this code in the small intestine, the long quiet coil behind the navel that takes what you have eaten and decides, slowly, what of it will become you. It is the body's room of conversion. Food goes in, and what was outside crosses over and becomes the warmth in your hands, the strength in your legs, the fire under the ribs that lets you keep going.

The shadow has its bodily floor here. Compromise sits in the gut. A small clench somewhere behind the navel each time you say yes to the smaller version of the day. Over years it shows up as a belly that does not run hot, an appetite that has gone a little vague, energy that does not arrive when it should. The wagon leaks lower down than the mind. The body knows it is taking in good food and turning it into less than it should.

The climb out is gut-level too. Warmth comes back to the belly first. Hunger sharpens. There is a steadiness behind the navel that was not there before, a quiet engine running clean. The old teachers called it the fire in the belly because that is exactly what it is, not a metaphor but a place inside you that either burns or does not. When the yeses become true again, it burns.
amino_acid:
Deeper than the organ, this code answers to Lysine, the same amino acid that runs under the first card. Lysine is one of the few the body cannot make for itself. It has to be taken in, broken down, and put to work. Among the many things it does, one is worth naming here. Lysine is what the body uses to build carnitine, the small molecule that carries fat into the engine of the cell where it is burned for energy. Without it, the fuel never reaches the fire.

There is a teaching in that, and it is the quiet shock of this card. The fire in the belly is not metaphor and it is not willpower. It is a chemistry that depends on something taken in from outside, used to ferry fuel to the place where heat is made. Compromise starves the carrier. Competence feeds it. The code runs all the way down to this: a fire that will not burn until what is needed has been received and carried in.
